behavioral_notes.element: AuthorizeAPI._make_request -> POST https://api.authorize.net/xml/v1/request.api (live) / https://apitest.authorize.net/xml/v1/request.api (test) using requests.post with merchantAuthentication block
behavioral_notes.observation: All Authorize.Net API calls route through AuthorizeAPI._make_request in models/authorize_request.py. The URL is selected at AuthorizeAPI.__init__ time: provider.state=='enabled' maps to api.authorize.net, otherwise apitest.authorize.net. Every request wraps a merchantAuthentication block containing authorize_login (name) and authorize_transaction_key (transactionKey). The body is JSON-serialised via json.dumps and posted with Python requests.post with a 60-second timeout. Error detection reads messages.resultCode=='Error' from the JSON response and additionally collects transactionResponse.errors for transaction-level errors; the consolidated error is returned as {'err_code':..., 'err_msg':...}. Unlike other acquirers that delegate to payment.provider._send_api_request, this module uses requests directly (sdk_imports=['requests'] per frontend extractor). The dual-URL test/live routing, the raw requests usage, and the merchantAuthentication embedding are invisible from model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._authorize_create_transaction_request + _send_payment_request -> AuthorizeAPI.authorize (authOnlyTransaction) vs AuthorizeAPI.auth_and_capture (authCaptureTransaction) branching on capture_manually and operation
behavioral_notes.observation: Authorize.Net supports a full authorize-then-capture split. The inline-form path (_authorize_create_transaction_request) and the off-session token path (_send_payment_request) both branch on provider.capture_manually: when True the API call is authorize() -> 'authOnlyTransaction' (places an auth hold, tx state -> authorized via _apply_updates x_type='auth_only'); when False it calls auth_and_capture() -> 'authCaptureTransaction' (settles immediately, tx -> done via x_type='auth_capture'). Validation operations always use authorize() regardless of capture_manually. For token payments (off-session), _prepare_tx_data builds a 'profile' block using token.authorize_profile (customerProfileId) and token.provider_ref (paymentProfileId); for new card/ACH payments it uses the 'payment.opaqueData' block from the Accept.js nonce. The billTo block (firstName/lastName/company/address/city/state/zip/country, all length-capped per Authorize API limits) is included only for non-profile requests. _apply_updates maps x_response_code '1' (Approved) by x_type: auth_capture/prior_auth_capture -> _set_done; auth_only -> _set_authorized (then _void for validation); void -> _set_done (refund/validation) or _set_canceled; refund -> _set_done + trigger cron. Code '2' -> _set_canceled; code '4' -> _set_pending; else -> _set_error. This authorize/capture split and the profile vs opaqueData divergence are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._send_refund_request -> stateful refund-or-void decision based on getTransactionDetailsRequest transactionStatus
behavioral_notes.observation: Refund logic in _send_refund_request first calls AuthorizeAPI.get_transaction_details (getTransactionDetailsRequest) to fetch the current transactionStatus of the source transaction. The status is then matched against const.TRANSACTION_STATUS_MAPPING: if 'voided' -> _set_canceled (funds never moved, no API call needed); if 'refunded' (refundPendingSettlement / refundSettledSuccessfully) -> _set_done and trigger cron post-processing; if 'authorized' (authorizedPendingCapture / capturedPendingSettlement) -> void() instead of refund because the payment has not settled yet (no refundTransaction needed); if 'captured' (settledSuccessfully) -> refund() which POSTs 'refundTransaction' with the masked cardNumber from tx_details and expirationDate='XXXX'. The void path creates no child tx; the refund path returns x_type='refund' and _set_done triggers cron post-processing. This stateful refund-or-void decision tree is entirely invisible from model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._extract_token_values -> AuthorizeAPI.create_customer_profile (two-step: createCustomerProfileFromTransactionRequest + getCustomerPaymentProfileRequest) -> payment.token (authorize_profile, provider_ref, payment_details)
behavioral_notes.observation: After a successful charge with tokenize=True, _extract_token_values calls AuthorizeAPI.create_customer_profile(partner, provider_reference). This makes two sequential API calls: (1) createCustomerProfileFromTransactionRequest using the transId and a merchantCustomerId of 'ODOO-{partner.id}-{uuid4()[:8]}'[:20] -- creating a customer + payment profile in Auth.Net from the completed transaction; (2) getCustomerPaymentProfileRequest to retrieve the masked card/bank account number (creditCard.cardNumber[-4:] or bankAccount.accountNumber[-4:] for the last-4 payment_details). The result yields authorize_profile (customerProfileId stored on payment.token.authorize_profile), provider_ref (customerPaymentProfileId stored on payment.token.provider_ref), and payment_details (last 4 digits). Subsequent off-session charges use these two IDs in the 'profile' block of _prepare_tx_data. If _extract_token_values is called on an existing-token transaction (self.token_id set), it returns {} immediately to avoid creating a duplicate profile. The two-call profile creation, the UUID merchant customer ID, and the dual-ID token structure are invisible to field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment_form.js: Accept.js client-side tokenization + /payment/authorize/payment jsonrpc route; controller row-lock anti-concurrent pattern
behavioral_notes.observation: The browser-side flow is driven by a patch on PaymentForm.prototype (static/src/interactions/payment_form.js). On 'authorize' provider selection, _prepareInlineForm loads the Accept.js SDK from https://js.authorize.net/v1/Accept.js in live mode or https://jstest.authorize.net/v1/Accept.js in test mode via loadJS. On payment submit, _processDirectFlow assembles a secureData object with authData (apiLoginID=authorize_login, clientKey=authorize_client_key) plus either cardData (cardNumber/month/year/cardCode) or bankData (nameOnAccount/accountNumber/routingNumber/accountType) read from the inline form inputs. Accept.dispatchData(secureData, callback) sends this to Authorize.Net's Accept.js SDK which returns a one-time-use opaqueData nonce (dataDescriptor + dataValue) without card/bank details ever touching the Odoo server (SAQ A-EP PCI scope). The nonce is then posted to /payment/authorize/payment via rpc with an access_token. In the controller AuthorizeController.authorize_payment validates the HMAC access_token (check_access_token(access_token, reference, partner_id)), then executes SELECT FOR NO KEY UPDATE to lock the transaction row against concurrent cron updates before calling _authorize_create_transaction_request -- preventing the single-use OTS token from being consumed twice. All of this client-side tokenization, SDK loading, and row-locking are invisible to Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: payment_authorize (Authorize.Net acquirer adapter for the payment engine; _inherit-only, no own models/views)
software_services: /payment/authorize/payment (jsonrpc, public: receives Accept.js opaqueData nonce + access_token; row-locks the tx via SELECT FOR NO KEY UPDATE; calls _authorize_create_transaction_request; processes response synchronously)

external_integrations.sdk: Accept.js (browser card/ACH tokenization); server side uses Python requests library directly (not via payment.provider._send_api_request)
external_integrations.auth: merchantAuthentication block in every JSON request body: name=authorize_login, transactionKey=authorize_transaction_key
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: server-to-server REST via Python requests (not delegated to the payment engine) to api.authorize.net XML/JSON API authenticated with a login/transactionKey block in every request body; a parallel client-side Accept.js tokenization channel (SAQ A-EP); no inbound webhook -- all state transitions are synchronous responses to the single /payment/authorize/payment route.

capabilities: Accept Card payments (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover) via Authorize.Net inline form with Accept.js client-side tokenization (SAQ A-EP)
Accept ACH/eCheck bank-account payments via Authorize.Net inline form with Accept.js bank tokenization
Manual authorize-then-capture split (support_manual_capture='full_only'): place auth hold, capture later
Full refund support (support_refund='full_only'): stateful void-or-refund based on Authorize.Net transaction status
Tokenization / Saved Cards and bank accounts (support_tokenization=True): vault customerProfileId + paymentProfileId for off-session recurring charges
Merchant self-configuration: action_update_merchant_details fetches authorize_client_key and available currencies directly from Auth.Net API
value_streams: Collect-Payment (new card/ACH, direct): Accept.js tokenize -> opaqueData nonce -> /payment/authorize/payment jsonrpc (row-locked) -> AuthorizeAPI.auth_and_capture or authorize -> POST api.authorize.net -> _process -> done/authorized/pending
Collect-Payment (off-session token): _send_payment_request -> AuthorizeAPI.authorize/auth_and_capture with profile block -> POST api.authorize.net -> _process -> done/authorized
Authorize-then-Capture: payment -> authorized state -> _send_capture_request -> priorAuthCaptureTransaction -> done
Refund: _send_refund_request -> getTransactionDetails (status check) -> void (if authorized/pending settlement) or refundTransaction (if settled) -> done/canceled
Tokenize: successful charge + tokenize flag -> _extract_token_values -> two Auth.Net API calls -> vault payment.token (customerProfileId + paymentProfileId + last4)

Access token validation: /payment/authorize/payment verifies HMAC check_access_token(reference, partner_id) before processing

Stateful refund-or-void: refund is issued only when transactionStatus is settledSuccessfully; earlier states trigger a void instead
Credentials gated: authorize_transaction_key and authorize_signature_key restricted to base.group_system

Authorize.Net (external acquirer / PSP for US, Australia, Canada)
Accountant (consumes settled/refunded payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_authorize is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: its purpose is to interconnect the payer (cardholder / bank account holder) and the merchant by linking the merchant to the Authorize.Net card/ACH network in the US, Australia, and Canada. Mediating-technology activities present: network contract management (API-key + credential management, single-currency constraint, client-key fetch), service provisioning (creating, capturing, voiding, and refunding Authorize.Net transactions per event), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.authorize.net link and the Accept.js client-side tokenization channel). Does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). activity_class is 'support' because payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash.

standard_capabilities: inline Card payment (Visa/MC/Amex/Discover) via Accept.js client-side tokenization (SAQ A-EP)
inline ACH/eCheck bank-account payment via Accept.js bank tokenization
full refund with stateful void-or-refund decision (full_only)
saved card/ACH tokenization (customerProfileId + paymentProfileId vault) for off-session recurring charges
merchant self-configuration: fetch client key and available currencies from Auth.Net API
typical_fits: US/AU/CA online shop or portal checkout accepting cards and ACH bank transfers via Authorize.Net
businesses requiring authorize-then-capture (e.g. ship-then-capture or service-then-bill models)
subscription or recurring billing using saved card/ACH tokens (off-session _send_payment_request)
single-currency merchants (one Authorize.Net account = one currency)
pay-invoice-online collection with account_payment / sale downstream
common_gaps: single currency only: one Authorize.Net account handles one currency; multiple currencies require multiple provider records

no inbound webhook for asynchronous settlement notification: all state transitions are synchronous from the /payment/authorize/payment route; Held-for-Review (status_code=4) maps to pending but is never auto-resolved
no partial capture or partial refund (full_only only)
authorize_signature_key is stored but not used in any signing or verification in the current code (no webhook signature verification implemented)
Accept.js CDN dependency means a live internet connection is needed during checkout
reconciliation and settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here

curl -X POST https://<host>/payment/authorize/payment (jsonrpc) without valid access_token -> expect ValidationError 'Received tampered payment request data.'

open_questions: authorize_signature_key is stored (base.group_system) but no code in the current module uses it for webhook signature verification -- is webhook/Silent Post notification handling expected in a future patch, or is this field legacy?
Held-for-Review (x_response_code='4') maps to _set_pending but no cron or route resolves it automatically; what is the operational process for reviewing and capturing/voiding held transactions?
Real-world distribution of card vs ACH payments and tokenization usage (no runtime row counts captured).
How multi-currency merchants are expected to configure this given the single-currency constraint (multiple provider records, one per currency).
Whether partial capture or partial refund is ever needed; support_manual_capture='full_only' and support_refund='full_only' rule those out at the engine level.
